action_items: Please review the fix applied in /app/backend/routes/export_import.py::_run_import_job — the preload cursor projection previously included both 'fields.<match_by>' AND 'fields' which MongoDB rejects with 'Path collision at fields' (code 31250). Because that MongoDB error was raised OUTSIDE the try/except in _run_import_job (during the 'Preload existing records by match_by' block), the asyncio background task died silently: the import_job status stayed 'running' forever, processed=0, and the 5-concurrent-imports guard eventually blocked further runs with 429 too_many_running. Fix: only add 'fields': 1 to the projection when match_by == 'record_number' (no path collision in that case). Consider additionally wrapping the entire body of _run_import_job in the top-level try/except so any future silent failure marks the job as 'failed' instead of hanging.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/export_import.py::_run_import_job — the pre-loop preparation (parse rows, load field_defs, preload existing_by_key, preload tag_map) all happens BEFORE the try/except. Any exception in that ~40-line prep block leaves the import_jobs doc stuck in status='running' forever and eats up a slot in the 5-concurrent guard. Wrap the whole body in try/except so failures are recorded as 'failed'.

routes/export_import.py::_run_import_job also creates the asyncio task via `asyncio.create_task(_run_import_job(...))` from within a FastAPI request handler — if uvicorn hot-reloads while a job is running, the task is cancelled without updating status. Consider moving to APScheduler or a real background worker for production, or at minimum recover 'running' jobs older than N minutes on startup.

routes/export_import.py::export_records — audit diff includes filters={q, category_id, tag_ids} but not columns=... or the resolved record count when limit truncates. For the bulk endpoint the review request asked for diff.kind='bulk' — verified present.

routes/export_import.py::_record_number uses `record_seq` field in the increment but the entity_types collection actually stores `record_counter` (visible on GET /entity-types/:id). Two counters end up running independently: `record_counter` (used by manual POST /records via routes/data.py) and `record_seq` (used only by import). Not a bug per se — but the two counters can collide (both start at PROD-000001) creating duplicate record_number values within an org. Consider using the same counter.
routes/shares.py — bcrypt cost=10 (~50 ms), 5-attempt window=60 s per (IP, share). Not per (IP) globally, so an attacker rotating share tokens is not rate-limited. Acceptable for MVP.

routes/shares.py::update_share — audit diff includes 'password_hash' key when password rotates because we build `updates['password_hash']` then log diff excluding password_hash — verified stripped in the audit line. Good.

rca of the issue:
Bug: POST /api/entity-types/{et_id}/records/import/execute would return job_id=queued but the job would never progress past processed=0, staying 'running' forever. After 5 such runs, subsequent execute calls returned 429 too_many_running.
Root cause: In /app/backend/routes/export_import.py::_run_import_job, when the plan specified `match_by != 'record_number'` (e.g. 'sku'), the code built a MongoDB find projection of `{'fields.sku': 1, '_id': 1, 'record_number': 1, 'fields': 1}`. MongoDB rejects that projection with `OperationFailure: Path collision at fields (code 31250)` because it cannot combine a whole-field include ('fields') with a sub-field include ('fields.sku'). The `async for r in cursor:` line raised this OperationFailure, BUT the cursor iteration lived OUTSIDE the `try:` block (~L945-956 in the original file), so the exception propagated up out of the asyncio task without ever hitting the except clause that marks the job 'failed'. Since we hold a reference to the task in `_IMPORT_JOBS`, no 'task exception never retrieved' warning was emitted at any easily-visible time. The import_jobs doc stayed status='running' forever.
Reproduction: Log in as owner, POST /import/preview with a 3-row CSV, POST /import/plan with `options.match_by='sku'`, POST /import/execute, poll /imports/{job_id}/progress — status stays 'running', processed=0.
Mitigation applied: When `match_by != 'record_number'`, only project the specific sub-field (fields.{match_by}) + _id + record_number. When match_by == 'record_number', we can safely include 'fields' since there's no collision. Fix is a 5-line change in routes/export_import.py.
Recommendation (not applied): move the pre-loop preparation inside a top-level try/except in _run_import_job so any future silent failure updates status='failed' + error_message instead of hanging.
